question: How many shifts does the SOC run each day and how long is each, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
evidence_quote: operates 24 hours a day in three 8-hour shifts

question: When does the weekly on-call rota change over, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
evidence_quote: changes on Monday at 09:00 local time

question: How quickly must an on-call analyst be able to reach a secure workstation, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
evidence_quote: reach a secure workstation within 45 minutes

question: How often may an analyst be on call, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
answer: No more than one week in three.
evidence_quote: No analyst is on call for more than one week in three

question: How far in advance must rota swaps be agreed, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
evidence_quote: agreed at least 48 hours in advance

question: Within how long must the on-call analyst acknowledge a page, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
evidence_quote: must acknowledge a page within 15 minutes

question: How much rest does an analyst get after a night call-out longer than 4 hours, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
answer: At least 11 hours before the next shift.
evidence_quote: at least 11 hours of rest before the next shift

question: Is a handover by message alone acceptable, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
answer: No, a live handover of about 15 minutes is required.
evidence_quote: A handover by message alone is not accepted

question: When may the outgoing analyst leave after handover, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
answer: Only after the incoming analyst replies Accepted in the ticket.
evidence_quote: only after the incoming analyst replies Accepted in the ticket

question: May credentials be written in handover notes, according to the AIT On-Call and Shift Handover Procedure (AIT-IR-PRC-015)?
answer: No; passwords and recovery codes are never written there.
evidence_quote: Passwords and recovery codes are never written in handover notes
